mainTopic: How much frankincense (לבונה) must remain to be burned, when extra frankincense disqualifies, and the start of the משנה on wrong intentions during the קמיצה.
overview: The גמרא begins by settling a contradiction in רבי שמעון's view about frankincense (לבונה) that shrank. It gives two answers: either the ברייתא really says 'a pinch', or one ruling is about frankincense with a מנחה and the other is about frankincense on its own. רבי יצחק בר יוסף, quoting רבי יוחנן, then lists three opinions on how much must be left to burn: the full קומץ (רבי מאיר), two pinches (רבי יהודה), or one pinch (רבי שמעון). All three come from the same פסוק. He adds that the argument is only about frankincense brought with a מנחה. Frankincense brought by itself, and the frankincense in the בזיכין of the לחם הפנים, must stay complete according to everyone, though רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא argue about frankincense brought by itself. Next, רמי בר חמא explains that too much frankincense disqualifies only when a whole second קומץ was set aside. He rules that extra frankincense becomes fixed with the offering only at the קמיצה, or at the actual removal of the בזיכין. A new משנה then begins about wrong intentions during the קמיצה. Planning to eat or burn the offering outside makes it פסול without כרת, and the list of 'next day' intentions continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: A teaching that seems to contradict רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says a קומץ of frankincense missing even a tiny amount is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: a handful of frankincense that is missing any amount at all is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier view of רבי שמעון that even one pinch of frankincense left over is enough. It brings a ברייתא where he seems to demand the whole amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one pinch is enough, then a handful missing a little should certainly still be fine. Yet this ברייתא says a handful missing even a tiny bit is פסול. So רבי שמעון seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A handful: the measured amount the כהן takes
Frankincense, burned on the מזבח
Disqualified, not valid as an offering

phrases.english: But isn't it taught (Rabbi Shimon says):
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in round brackets. Either way, the challenge is aimed at רבי שמעון's view.

phrases.aramaic: קוֹמֶץ לְבוֹנָה שֶׁחָסַר כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: A handful of frankincense that is missing any amount at all is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's earlier view that one pinch remaining is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that one קורט of frankincense remaining is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying a handful missing any amount is disqualified. That means the whole amount is needed, which contradicts the one-pinch view.

steps.title: First answer: read 'pinch' instead of 'handful'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא so that it talks about a קורט (pinch) that is missing anything, not a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: a pinch of frankincense that is missing any amount at all is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word in the ברייתא. It says the ברייתא really means a 'pinch', not a 'handful'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's minimum is one pinch. So the ברייתא is only saying that if even that last pinch is missing a bit, it is פסול. Now there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A pinch: a tiny amount of frankincense
Was missing, became less
Any amount at all, even the smallest

phrases.english: Teach it this way:

phrases.aramaic: קוֹרֶט לְבוֹנָה שֶׁחָסַר כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: A pinch of frankincense that is missing any amount at all is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 1 by correcting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a full handful must remain, which goes against רבי שמעון's one-pinch view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says a pinch, which is רבי שמעון's minimum. If even that is missing a bit, it is פסול.

steps.title: Second answer: frankincense with a מנחה versus frankincense on its own
steps.stepSummary: Without changing the text, the גמרא says the two rulings of רבי שמעון are about two different kinds of frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: here it is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering, and there it is about frankincense that comes by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps the ברייתא as it is. It splits the cases: one pinch is enough for frankincense brought with a מנחה. Frankincense brought by itself must be complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both statements of רבי שמעון are true, each for its own case. Frankincense that is part of a מנחה is more flexible. Frankincense brought as an offering on its own may not be missing anything.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces a second, different answer
That comes together with a meal offering
By itself, as its own offering
A meal offering, made of flour

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
here, it is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is רבי שמעון's earlier view, that one pinch left is enough.

phrases.english: there, it is about frankincense that comes by itself.
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the ברייתא from step 1, where the full handful is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second way to answer step 1's challenge, different from the answer in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seem to be about the same frankincense, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: One pinch is enough for frankincense brought with a מנחה. Frankincense brought by itself must be complete.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 3 does not depend on step 2. It is a separate answer that leaves the ברייתא's wording as it is.

steps.title: Three opinions on how much frankincense must remain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there are three opinions: the full קומץ (רבי מאיר), two pinches (רבי יהודה), or one pinch (רבי שמעון).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: there are three opinions on this. רבי מאיר holds: a handful at the start and a handful at the end. רבי יהודה holds: a handful at the start and two pinches at the end. רבי שמעון holds: a handful at the start and one pinch at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement lays out the three תנאים side by side. All agree the כהן starts with a full handful. They argue about how much must still be left when it is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'At the start' means the amount brought with the offering. 'At the end' means the minimum that must still be there when it is burned on the מזבח. רבי מאיר is the strictest, then רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון is the most lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A disagreement, a dispute
At the start, when the frankincense is first brought
At the end, when it is burned
Pinches (plural of קורט)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
There are three opinions on this matter.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: קוֹמֵץ בַּתְּחִילָּה וְקוֹמֵץ בַּסּוֹף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: a handful at the start and a handful at the end;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: קוֹמֶץ בַּתְּחִילָּה וּשְׁנֵי קְרָטִין בַּסּוֹף,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds: a handful at the start and two pinches at the end;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: קוֹמֶץ בַּתְּחִילָּה וְקוֹרֶט אֶחָד בַּסּוֹף.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon holds: a handful at the start and one pinch at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שָׁלֹשׁ מַחְלוֹקֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the contradiction to a clear list of all three opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All start with a full קומץ. At the end, רבי מאיר needs the full קומץ, רבי יהודה needs two pinches, and רבי שמעון needs one pinch.
steps.whatToRemember: Full handful (רבי מאיר), two pinches (רבי יהודה), one pinch (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: All three opinions come from one פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Each תנא reads 'ואת כל הלבונה אשר על המנחה' differently, and that gives his opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: All three learned their view from one פסוק: 'And all the frankincense that is upon the meal offering.' רבי מאיר holds that it must be the frankincense that was set with the מנחה from the start, meaning all of it. רבי יהודה holds: 'all' can mean even one pinch, and 'את' adds another pinch. רבי שמעון does not learn anything from 'את'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where each opinion comes from. All three are reading the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'all the frankincense' as the whole original amount. רבי יהודה reads 'כל' as 'any part, even one pinch' and treats 'את' as adding a second pinch, which makes two. רבי שמעון agrees about 'כל' but learns nothing from 'את', so he stays at one pinch.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse
They explained the verse to learn a law from it
Was set, was fixed (as the amount)
From the start, originally
To include something extra
A small word in the פסוק that some תנאים use to include something extra

phrases.english: And all three of them learned it from one verse:
"And all the frankincense that is upon the meal offering."

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: עַד דְּאִיתָא לִלְבוֹנָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: not until there is the frankincense
phrases.notes: He means it cannot be burned until all of that frankincense is still there.

phrases.english: that was set together with the meal offering from the start.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: ״כׇּל״ – וַאֲפִילּוּ חַד קוֹרֶט,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: "all" means even one pinch;
"et" is to include another pinch.
And Rabbi Shimon does not learn anything from "et".
phrases.notes: He agrees with רבי יהודה about 'כל', so for him one pinch is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for each of the three opinions in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כל' means the whole original amount (רבי מאיר) or any part, even one pinch (רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון). 'את' adds a second pinch for רבי יהודה only.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one extra little word, 'את', can be the whole difference between two תנאים.

steps.title: The argument is only about frankincense brought with a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the argument: frankincense brought by itself must stay a full קומץ, according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the argument is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering. But for frankincense that comes by itself, everyone agrees: a handful at the start and a handful at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement from the same speaker limits where the argument applies. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are lenient only when the frankincense comes with a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Frankincense brought by itself must have the full handful left at the end, even for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. This fits the second answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
But: marks the case that is different

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The argument is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering,
but about frankincense that comes by itself,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל קוֹמֶץ בַּתְּחִילָּה וְקוֹמֶץ בַּסּוֹף.
phrases.english: everyone agrees: a handful at the start and a handful at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּלְבוֹנָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the three-way argument of steps 4–5 to frankincense brought with a מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Frankincense brought by itself must remain a full קומץ, according to everyone.

steps.title: Why the פסוק says 'that is upon the meal offering'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר על המנחה' teach that the leniency applies only to frankincense with a מנחה, not to frankincense on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why 'that is upon the meal offering' was needed: with a מנחה, yes; by itself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where in the פסוק the difference from step 6 comes from. The words 'upon the meal offering' limit the leniency to frankincense that comes with a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כל' and 'את' allow burning even with only a pinch or two left. But 'אשר על המנחה' ties that leniency to frankincense brought with a מנחה. Frankincense brought by itself gets no leniency and must be complete.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason, for this purpose
It was needed (the extra words in the פסוק)
Together with
Yes / no

phrases.english: For this the words "that is upon the meal offering" were needed:
that together with a meal offering, yes,
phrases.notes: Yes, it may be burned even with only a pinch or two left.

phrases.english: by itself, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the limit stated in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that frankincense brought by itself must remain a full קומץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'אשר על המנחה' in ויקרא 6:8
steps.whatToRemember: The leniency of one or two pinches applies only to frankincense brought with a מנחה. Frankincense brought by itself must stay a full קומץ, according to everyone.

steps.title: The frankincense of the shewbread bowls needs two full handfuls according to everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument is only about לבונה brought with a מנחה. The לבונה in the בזיכין must be two full קמצין from start to finish according to all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the argument is only about frankincense that comes with a מנחה. But the frankincense in the bowls (with the לחם הפנים) must be two handfuls at the start and two handfuls at the end, according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: Another limit on the argument: רבי יוחנן says the frankincense of the לחם הפנים is not part of the argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון allow a shrunken amount of לבונה for a מנחה. Here we learn that this leniency does not reach the בזיכין: there, two full קמצין are needed at the start and still at the end. So even רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון agree in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The two bowls of frankincense placed next to the לחם הפנים
Handfuls (plural of קוֹמֶץ)
Everyone agrees
Argument, dispute

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The argument is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering,
but about frankincense that comes in bowls,
phrases.notes: These are the two bowls of לבונה set out with the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: everyone agrees: two handfuls at the beginning,
and two handfuls at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּלְבוֹנָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case (בזיכין) that is outside the argument, parallel to לבונה by itself in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לבונה of the בזיכין requires two full קמצין at the start and at the end, according to all opinions.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say this at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement as unnecessary, and is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency of one or two pinches comes from 'כל' (and 'את') in the פסוק about a מנחה, and step 7 showed that 'אשר על המנחה' limits it to frankincense brought with a מנחה. The לבונה of the בזיכין is not 'on a מנחה', so it seems clear it gets no leniency. Why say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why did this need to be said?

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The leniency only applies to frankincense 'אשר על המנחה', so the bowls should obviously not be included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the statement in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement about the בזיכין (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on step 7, only לבונה 'on a מנחה' gets the leniency, so the בזיכין are clearly excluded and the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: Because it comes with bread, you might think it counts as 'on the מנחה'
steps.stepSummary: The statement was needed: since the בזיכין come with the לחם הפנים, one might think they count like לבונה on a מנחה. רבי יוחנן teaches they don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it comes together with bread, it is like 'that which is on the מנחה'. So he teaches us it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake רבי יוחנן's statement prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים is bread, a little like a מנחה, so one might think its frankincense counts as 'אשר על המנחה' and gets the leniency. רבי יוחנן teaches that it does not: the בזיכין still need two full handfuls.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought...
He teaches us (that it is not so)
Together with
It is similar to, counts like

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּבַהֲדֵי לֶחֶם אָתְיָא,
phrases.english: You might have said: since it comes together with bread,
phrases.notes: The bread is the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: it is like 'that which is on the meal offering',
so he teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּבַהֲדֵי לֶחֶם אָתְיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the statement prevents a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בזיכין come with bread, their לבונה might count as 'אשר על המנחה' and get the leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בזיכין do not count as 'on the מנחה'; two full קמצין are required by all.
steps.whatToRemember: Two cases are outside the argument for רבי יוחנן: לבונה brought by itself, and the לבונה of the בזיכין. In both, the full amount is needed according to everyone.

steps.title: Two אמוראים argue about frankincense brought by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא argue: one says לבונה by itself must be a full קומץ according to all; the other says the same argument applies there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree about this. One says: the argument is about frankincense that comes with a מנחה, but frankincense that comes by itself needs a full handful at the start and at the end, according to everyone. The other says: just as there is an argument here, there is an argument there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי יוחנן's limit from step 6 is itself argued about by two later אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view matches step 6: לבונה by itself gets no leniency. The second view says the תנאים argue about לבונה by itself in the same way, so רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון would allow less there too.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
By itself, on its own

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha disagree about it.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the case of frankincense brought by itself, from step 6.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּלְבוֹנָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: One said: the argument is about frankincense that comes with a meal offering,
but about frankincense that comes by itself,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל קוֹמֶץ בַּתְּחִילָּה וְקוֹמֶץ בַּסּוֹף,
phrases.english: everyone agrees: a handful at the beginning and a handful at the end.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזוֹ כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזוֹ.
phrases.english: And one said: just as there is an argument in this case, so there is an argument in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the case of לבונה by itself (step 6) and shows it is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא: לבונה by itself needs a full קומץ according to all. The other: the תנאים argue about it just like לבונה with a מנחה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two people named רבי יצחק: רבי יצחק בר יוסף (step 8) passes on רבי יוחנן's words, while רבי יצחק נפחא is one side of this argument.

steps.title: The משנה implies extra frankincense is fine, but a ברייתא says it disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says lacking לבונה disqualifies, implying extra is fine. A ברייתא says extra לבונה disqualifies too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'he made its frankincense less'. That implies that if he added extra, it is fit. But a ברייתא teaches: if he added extra, it is unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic on the משנה's words 'חיסר לבונתה' and challenges what they imply using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only too little לבונה as a problem, so it sounds like too much is fine. The ברייתא openly says too much לבונה also makes the מנחה unfit. These two seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it less, put in too little
Extra, too much
Fit, valid
Unfit, disqualified

phrases.english: The משנה says: 'he made its frankincense less',
which implies that if he added extra, it is fit.
But a ברייתא teaches: if extra, it is unfit!

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיסֵּר לְבוֹנָתָהּ – הָא יָתֵיר כְּשֵׁרָה, וְהָתַנְיָא: יָתֵיר פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the shrunken-קומץ argument to a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: What the משנה's words 'חיסר לבונתה' imply
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies extra לבונה is fit, but a ברייתא states that extra לבונה disqualifies.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about setting aside two handfuls
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the ברייתא's 'extra' means he set aside two full קמצין for the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: the ברייתא is talking about a case where he set aside two handfuls for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the clash by narrowing what the ברייתא means by 'extra'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A little extra frankincense is fine, matching the משנה. The ברייתא only disqualifies when he set aside a whole second קומץ, so the משנה and ברייתא are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside, designated
For example, in a case where

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
It is a case where he set aside two handfuls for it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מנחה: he put two full handfuls of לבונה on it instead of one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי קְמָצִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any extra לבונה at all disqualifies, which clashes with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only setting aside two full קמצין disqualifies; a little extra is fit, as the משנה implies.

steps.title: Two handfuls of frankincense, one lost: before or after the קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that if one of two קמצין of לבונה is lost before the קמיצה, they were never fixed with the מנחה. If it is lost after the קמיצה, they were already fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר חמא said: If someone set aside two handfuls of לבונה for a מנחה and one of them got lost, it depends on timing. If it was lost before the קמיצה, the two were not yet fixed with the מנחה. If it was lost after the קמיצה, they were already fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא adds a ruling about the case from step 13, two full קמצין of לבונה for one מנחה, when one of them gets lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two full קמצין is too much לבונה and disqualifies the מנחה, but only once that amount is 'fixed' with it. The fixing moment is the קמיצה. If one was lost before then, only one handful remains and the מנחה is fine. If it was lost after, the extra amount was already locked in, so losing it later does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside, designated
The כהן's act of taking a handful from the מנחה
They became fixed (locked in) together with the offering
Handfuls (here, handfuls of לבונה)

phrases.english: And Rami bar Chama said:
If he set aside two handfuls for it,
phrases.notes: 'For it' means for the מנחה. The handfuls are of לבונה, as in the previous step.

phrases.english: and one of them got lost
before the taking of the handful, they were not fixed,
after the taking of the handful, they were fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הִפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי קְמָצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רמי בר חמא's case of two full קמצין by setting the moment the extra לבונה becomes fixed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra לבונה is fixed with the מנחה at the קמיצה. A loss before then avoids disqualification; a loss after does not.

steps.title: Four handfuls for the two bowls of the showbread
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא gives the same kind of rule for the לחם הפנים. If two of four קמצין set aside for the two בזיכין are lost before the bowls are removed, nothing was fixed. If they are lost after, all four were fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר חמא said: If someone set aside four handfuls of לבונה for the two בזיכין, and two of them got lost, it depends on timing. Before the removal of the בזיכין, they were not fixed. After the removal of the בזיכין, they were fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא applies the same timing idea to the לבונה that sits in two bowls next to the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each bowl normally holds one קומץ, so four is double. For the לחם הפנים, the fixing moment is not a קמיצה but the removal (סילוק) of the bowls from the שולחן. A loss before removal leaves the normal amount; a loss after removal comes too late.

keyTerms.meaning: The two bowls of לבונה placed with the לחם הפנים
Removal (of the bowls from the שולחן)
The showbread on the שולחן in the מקדש

phrases.english: And Rami bar Chama said:
If he set aside four handfuls for the two bowls,
phrases.notes: Normally each bowl gets one handful, so four is twice the usual amount.

phrases.english: and two of them got lost
before the removal of the bowls, they were not fixed,
after the removal of the bowls, they were fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הִפְרִישׁ אַרְבָּעָה קְמָצִין לִשְׁנֵי בָּזִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same rule as step 14, applied to the בזיכין of the לחם הפנים, with removal of the bowls in place of the קמיצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra לבונה in the בזיכין is fixed at the removal of the bowls. A loss before removal avoids disqualification; a loss after does not.

steps.title: Why say the second ruling? It is the same as the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רמי בר חמא needed the ruling about the בזיכין, since it seems identical to his ruling about the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this one too? It is the same thing as that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the second ruling, because it seems to repeat the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the בזיכין plays the same role for the לחם הפנים that the קמיצה plays for a מנחה. So the rule 'fixed at that moment' should already be obvious from step 14. Why would רמי בר חמא say it twice?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this one too?
This is the same as that

phrases.english: Why do I need this one too?
It is the same as that one!
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the earlier ruling about the two handfuls for a מנחה (step 14).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether step 15 adds anything beyond step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רמי בר חמא's second ruling (step 15).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removal of the bowls is just like the קמיצה, so the second ruling looks redundant.

steps.title: The second ruling teaches that only the actual removal counts
steps.stepSummary: The second ruling is needed. One might think that since the לבונה of the לחם הפנים is already separate in its own bowl, once the time for removal arrives it counts as removed. רמי בר חמא teaches that only the actual removal fixes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since its handful is already clearly separate, once the time comes to remove it, it is as if it were already removed. So he teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 by showing a mistake we could have made about the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a מנחה, the קומץ only becomes separate when the כהן takes it, so the act clearly matters. By the לחם הפנים, the לבונה sits in its own bowl from the start. So we might think that once the time for removal arrives, it already counts as removed, and the extra handfuls are fixed even if they were lost before the bowls were actually taken off the שולחן. רמי בר חמא teaches that the extra handfuls are fixed only by the actual removal.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Clearly separate, already set apart
It is as if it were already removed
He teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Extra לבונה is fixed only at the real act: the קמיצה for a מנחה, and the actual removal of the בזיכין for the לחם הפנים. The arrival of the time for removal is not enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'the time to remove has come' is the same as 'it was removed.' The גמרא brings this as the mistake רמי בר חמא is correcting.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since its handful is already clearly separate,
phrases.notes: The לבונה of the לחם הפנים sits in its own bowl, unlike a מנחה where the כהן still has to take the handful out.

phrases.english: once the time has come to remove it,
it is as though it were already removed,
so he teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דִּבְרִיר קוֹמֶץ דִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Needed to reject a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the לבונה of the לחם הפנים is already separate, reaching the time of removal counts as removal, so a loss after that time would not help.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the actual removal of the בזיכין fixes the extra לבונה with the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Intending to eat or burn the meal offering outside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the כהן takes the קומץ while intending to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ or לבונה outside the עזרה, even just a כזית, the מנחה is פסול, but there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone takes the handful from a meal offering while planning to eat its leftovers outside, or even an olive-sized piece of the leftovers outside, or to burn its handful outside, or an olive-sized piece of its handful outside, or to burn its frankincense outside, the offering is unfit, but there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists wrong 'place' intentions during the קמיצה and rules that they ruin the מנחה but do not bring כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is only the כהן's plan, not anything he actually did. A plan to eat or burn the מנחה outside its proper place (חוץ למקומו) is enough to make it פסול, even if the plan covers just a כזית. But this kind of wrong thought does not make it פיגול, so someone who eats it is not liable to כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes the handful (קומץ) out of the מנחה, one of its main services
The leftover part of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken, eaten by the כהנים
An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount that counts
Intending to do something outside its proper place, here outside the עזרה
Unfit; the offering is ruined
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing was actually done outside. The כהן only had the wrong plan in mind while doing the קמיצה, and that thought alone is what makes it פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main contrast of the משנה: a wrong-place intention makes it only פסול, while a wrong-time intention (coming next) is more severe.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who takes a handful from the meal offering
with the intent to eat its leftovers outside,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means outside the Temple courtyard (עזרה), where the leftovers must be eaten.

phrases.english: or an olive-bulk of its leftovers outside,
to burn its handful outside,
or an olive-bulk of its handful outside,
or to burn its frankincense outside —
it is unfit, but there is no כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹמֵץ אֶת הַמִּנְחָה לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁיָרֶיהָ בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the discussion of רמי בר חמא's rulings about the לבונה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention during קמיצה to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ or לבונה outside the עזרה, even just a כזית, makes the מנחה פסול but brings no כרת.

steps.title: Intending to eat or burn the meal offering the next day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing the parallel cases of intending to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ or לבונה the next day. The ruling for these cases comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he planned to eat its leftovers the next day, or an olive-sized piece of its leftovers the next day, or to burn its handful the next day, or an olive-sized piece of its handful the next day, or to burn the frankincense the next day...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its second list: the same cases, but now the plan is about the wrong time instead of the wrong place. The ruling for this list comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case from the first list is repeated word for word, with 'outside' swapped for 'tomorrow'. This sets up an exact comparison. The only thing that changes is whether the wrong thought was about place (חוץ למקומו) or time (חוץ לזמנו), so any difference in the ruling comes from that change alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The next day, after the time allowed for eating or burning
Intending to do something after its allowed time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop reading here. This sentence is not finished, and the ruling for the 'tomorrow' cases comes right after.

phrases.english: To eat its leftovers the next day,
or an olive-bulk of its leftovers the next day,
to burn its handful the next day,
or an olive-bulk of its handful the next day,
or to burn the frankincense the next day —

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line (the second half of the משנה's case list, with the ruling still to come)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same list of cases from step 18, changing the wrong intention from place ('outside') to time ('tomorrow').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cases are listed here: intending to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ or לבונה the next day. The ruling is given in the continuation of the משנה.
